labels.text: Compare prices and upgrade on Web

S81.07.needs: a signed-in account (the list also opens signed out)
S81.07.note: No "1x" wording and no concrete allowance number was found in the plan copy; the baseline appears only by name in "Same usage as <plan>" (managed-usage-limits.ts:236) and in the multiplier lines.
steps: Press Cmd+Shift+P, type "Compare Plans" and choose "Code: Compare Plans".
Read the list. Each row shows the plan name, a usage line, and an Includes or Adds over line.
Find the usage line on the paid plans. Look for "Same usage as <plan>" or "<n>x more usage than <plan>" and check that the baseline plan is named.
Compare with Expected: a plan that is the baseline for 5x/15x should be named with its concrete allowance. The Free row says "A usage allowance, free models only".

S81.08.needs: a signed-in paid account is best to see the usage rows
S81.08.note: The code names only the 5-hour session window and the weekly window; the Expected monthly window is not in the code.
steps: Press Cmd+Shift+P, type "Compare Plans" and choose "Code: Compare Plans".
Read the usage line of a paid plan, for example "<n>x more usage per session and <m>x more weekly usage than <plan>".
Open Code: Account & Usage (Cmd+Shift+P) and read the usage rows "Current session" and "This week" for the windows.
Compare with Expected: the copy should name which allowance is multiplied, the current session window and the weekly window. No monthly window was found in the code.

labels.text: Compare prices and upgrade on Web

S81.09.needs: a signed-in account, ideally on a plan other than the top one, so that the "Adds over" line appears
S81.09.note: The feature list is built from billing-catalog.ts; the enforcement of each gate is inner behaviour and is not confirmed from the extension UI.
steps: Press Cmd+Shift+P, type "Compare Plans" and choose "Code: Compare Plans".
Read the detail line under each plan: "Includes: ...", "Adds over <plan>: ..." or "No features beyond <plan>".
Compare the feature lists between two plans and check that they differ in features as well as usage.
Compare with Expected: each difference should be listed. The server-side enforcement of each gate is not visible from the extension and needs the web app or a live test.

S81.14.needs: a Free account and a paid account, to compare which options are gated
S81.14.note: The Effort row and Switch model row were found in the action sheet; no plan gate on them was found in the code, and the server clamp is inner behaviour.
steps: Press Cmd+Shift+P, type "Open Actions" and choose "Code: Open Actions".
Under the "Model" separator, read the "Effort: <level>" row. Its description reads "Set reasoning effort (low / medium / high / max)".
Choose "Switch model…" and see which models are listed.

Compare with Expected: the Effort and model choice should be shown as gated options for some plans. The code does not show a plan gate on these rows, and the server-side clamp of each request is not visible from the UI.
S81.14.where: Command Palette > Code: Open Actions > Model > Effort: <level>

S81.15.needs: a paid account with a flagship weekly allowance; the cap-used message needs the allowance used up
S81.15.note: The admission block message is in billing-catalog.ts (flagship_weekly_limit_reached); the cap-used state is hard to reach from the UI and is not confirmed here.
steps: Press Cmd+Shift+P, type "Account & Usage" and choose "Code: Account & Usage".
Find the row labelled "Most capable models" with its usage and reset time.
Compare its description and limit with the weekly row "This week".

Compare with Expected: the flagship weekly cap should be shown separately and, when used up, the blocked-request message should appear. The row is shown only when the account has a flagship allowance.
S81.15.where: Command Palette > Code: Account & Usage > "Most capable models" row

labels.text: Paid Cloud capabilities are paused until billing is resolved

S81.25.needs: a paid account with a subscription that needs attention (for example a failed renewal), which the tester may not be able to create
S81.25.note: No grace-period rule for paid plans was found in the extension. Grace language exists only for enterprise contracts (packages/contracts/types/src/enterprise/contract-lifecycle.ts).
steps: Press Cmd+Shift+P, type "Account & Usage" and choose "Code: Account & Usage".
Look for a warning row "<plan> subscription: <status>" with the description "Paid Cloud capabilities are paused until billing is resolved".
Read the "Manage billing & subscription" row and its description.

Compare with Expected: a failed renewal should show what access remains and how to fix it. The extension shows only that paid capabilities are paused; no grace-period rule or grace length was found for paid plans.
S81.25.where: Command Palette > Code: Account & Usage > "<plan> subscription: <status>" warning row

S81.27.needs: the same account signed in on two surfaces (VS Code and the web)
S81.27.note: The extension reads the server plan through /api/usage (apps/extension-vscode/src/utils/api.ts); the sharing itself is inner behaviour seen only as matching values.
steps: Sign in to the VS Code extension with an account that has a paid plan.
Open Command Palette > Code: Account & Usage and note the "Plan: <name>" description on the "Cloud usage" or "Cloud quota" row.
Sign in to the same account on the web, and open its usage page.
Compare with Expected: both surfaces should show the same plan and usage. The per-surface server enforcement is not visible from the UI.
S81.27.where: Code: Account & Usage shows the plan name, same as the web app for the same account

labels.text: Compare prices and upgrade on Web

S81.28.needs: a signed-in account on a plan below the top plan
S81.28.note: The "why a blocked feature needs a plan" text is in packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts and was not confirmed as shown in VS Code.
steps: Press Cmd+Shift+P, type "Compare Plans" and choose "Code: Compare Plans".
Read the detail line of each plan. Plans above your plan show "Adds over <your plan>: <features>", and your plan shows its own features.
Open Code: Open Actions and find "Upgrade for higher capacity" (or run Code: Upgrade Your Plan) to see the upgrade prompt.
Compare with Expected: each plan should explain what it adds, and a blocked feature should say which plan it needs. The blocked-feature wording is in the server copy, not the extension.
S81.28.where: Command Palette > Code: Compare Plans, then the "Adds over" detail of each plan
